answer_rows.question: How long does the bank have to resolve a credit card billing error under Reg Z?
answer_rows.answer: The creditor must resolve the dispute within two complete billing cycles, and in no case later than 90 days after receiving the notice. [reg_z_summary#4] The cardholder must send a billing error notice so that the creditor receives it within 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement that reflected the error. [reg_z_summary#4]

answer_rows.question: Within how many days must a cardholder send a billing error notice?
answer_rows.answer: The cardholder must send a billing error notice so that the creditor receives it within 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement that reflected the error. [reg_z_summary#4] The creditor must send a written acknowledgment within 30 days of receiving the notice, unless it resolves the dispute within that period. [reg_z_summary#4] A consumer must give notice of an error within 60 days after the institution sent the periodic statement on which the error first appeared. [reg_e_summary#3]

answer_rows.question: What is the maximum liability for unauthorized use of a credit card?
answer_rows.answer: A cardholder's liability for unauthorized use of a credit card is capped at $50. [reg_z_summary#2] Sentinel Bank applies a zero-liability policy for confirmed unauthorized use, so customers are not charged that $50. [reg_z_summary#2]

answer_rows.question: What is the consumer liability if a lost debit card is reported within two business days?
answer_rows.answer: If the consumer fails to report an unauthorized transfer that appears on a periodic statement within 60 days after the statement was sent, the consumer can face unlimited liability for transfers that occur after the 60-day period and before notice, if the institution can show the transfers would not have occurred had the consumer reported in time. [reg_e_summary#2] If the consumer notifies the institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft, liability is limited to the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers made before notice. [reg_e_summary#2]

answer_rows.question: Under Regulation E, how quickly must the bank investigate an error and when is provisional credit needed?
answer_rows.answer: For unauthorized transactions under $500 on accounts older than 90 days, issue provisional credit within 2 business days. [dispute_handling_sop#3] For other disputes, issue provisional credit within 10 business days if the investigation is expected to take longer than 10 business days. [dispute_handling_sop#3]

answer_rows.question: When must an analyst begin reviewing a P1 alert?
answer_rows.answer: The card is temporarily blocked automatically and an analyst must begin review within 1 hour. [fraud_investigation_playbook#1] Review must begin within 4 business hours. [fraud_investigation_playbook#1]

answer_rows.question: What evidence must be collected for every fraud case?
answer_rows.answer: Every case summary must contain: the finding, the evidence relied on, the policy or regulation applied, the customer impact, and the analyst's name. [fraud_investigation_playbook#6]

answer_rows.question: What are strong indicators of card fraud?
answer_rows.answer: Escalate: send to the Fraud Operations lead when the total exposure exceeds $5,000, when an account-takeover is suspected, or when money-laundering indicators are present. [fraud_investigation_playbook#5] Confirmed fraud: block and reissue the card, credit the customer under the zero-liability policy, and file the case for chargeback recovery. [fraud_investigation_playbook#5]

answer_rows.question: When should a fraud case be escalated to the Fraud Operations lead?
answer_rows.answer: Escalate: send to the Fraud Operations lead when the total exposure exceeds $5,000, when an account-takeover is suspected, or when money-laundering indicators are present. [fraud_investigation_playbook#5] Confirmed fraud: block and reissue the card, credit the customer under the zero-liability policy, and file the case for chargeback recovery. answer_rows.question: How quickly must a written acknowledgment be sent after a dispute is received?
answer_rows.answer: The creditor must send a written acknowledgment within 30 days of receiving the notice, unless it resolves the dispute within that period. [reg_z_summary#4] The creditor must resolve the dispute within two complete billing cycles, and in no case later than 90 days after receiving the notice. [reg_z_summary#4]

answer_rows.question: When should provisional credit be issued for an unauthorized transaction under $500?
answer_rows.answer: For unauthorized transactions under $500 on accounts older than 90 days, issue provisional credit within 2 business days. [dispute_handling_sop#3] For other disputes, issue provisional credit within 10 business days if the investigation is expected to take longer than 10 business days. [dispute_handling_sop#3]

answer_rows.question: How long does a temporary card block last before it must be reviewed?
answer_rows.answer: The card is temporarily blocked automatically and an analyst must begin review within 1 hour. [fraud_investigation_playbook#1] Review must begin within 4 business hours. [fraud_investigation_playbook#1] A temporary block must be reviewed and either lifted or converted within 24 hours. [card_controls_policy#1]

answer_rows.question: How long does expedited card delivery take for confirmed fraud victims?
answer_rows.answer: Standard delivery takes 5 to 7 business days; expedited delivery (2 business days) is free for confirmed fraud victims. [card_controls_policy#2] When fraud is confirmed, or the customer reports a lost or stolen card, the card is permanently blocked and a new card with a new number is issued. [card_controls_policy#2]

answer_rows.question: What are the signals of an account takeover?
answer_rows.answer: Suspected account takeovers must be escalated to Fraud Operations and the customer's online credentials must be reset. [card_controls_policy#4] Escalate: send to the Fraud Operations lead when the total exposure exceeds $5,000, when an account-takeover is suspected, or when money-laundering indicators are present. [fraud_investigation_playbook#5]

answer_rows.question: Can I write the full card number in the case notes?
answer_rows.answer: Full card numbers must never be stored in case notes, tickets, emails or chat. [data_privacy_pii_policy#2]

answer_rows.question: What must happen to restricted data before text is sent to an external AI model?
answer_rows.answer: Restricted data must be removed or masked before any text is sent to an external AI model or service. [data_privacy_pii_policy#3] Confidential data may be sent to an approved AI provider only under a contract that prohibits training on the data and sets a retention period. [data_privacy_pii_policy#3]

answer_rows.question: Should we tell the customer about an AML referral?
answer_rows.answer: Do not tell the customer that an AML referral is being made. [aml_escalation_guidelines#2] Create an internal referral with the case ID, the transactions of concern and a factual description. [aml_escalation_guidelines#2]

answer_rows.question: Above what cash amount is a Currency Transaction Report required?
answer_rows.answer: Cash transactions above $10,000 require a Currency Transaction Report, so repeated amounts just below that level are a red flag. [aml_escalation_guidelines#1] Transactions that seem structured to stay just below reporting thresholds. [aml_escalation_guidelines#1]

answer_rows.question: Can an AI system make the final decision on a customer dispute?
answer_rows.answer: Human accountability: AI systems may recommend; a named employee makes and owns every decision that affects a customer. [ai_usage_and_model_risk_policy#1] If no source supports a statement, the system must say it does not know. [ai_usage_and_model_risk_policy#1]

answer_rows.question: What must evaluation sets for generative AI include?
answer_rows.answer: Evaluation sets must include adversarial cases such as prompt injection and out-of-scope questions. [ai_usage_and_model_risk_policy#3]
